messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels lighter now—less noise, fewer whispers. The usual channels hum along as if nothing’s changed, and even the embassies seem untroubled. But let’s not mistake quiet for stillness; the walls still have ears, and the old rules still apply. Stay sharp, stay small, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual tension, more like something shifting beneath the surface. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our circles tight and our steps careful; the regime’s grip may be slipping, but it’s not gone yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms in sight, but the forecast is tricky. Best to keep your boots clean and your supplies in order, just in case the wind shifts. Stay sharp, but no need to rush."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. But even the strongest roots can dry out if the rains don’t come. Keep your gardens tended, and trust only the hands you’ve known for years."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like a storm coming, more like the calm before something unspoken. The usual routines hold, but the way people watch the news, the way the guards stand just a little less tall, the way even the loyalists whisper *‘when’* instead of *‘if’*—it’s not proof of anything, but it’s not nothing either. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust your own eyes more than the headlines."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, just the usual wind. The farmers are planting for the long season, and the markets are busy as ever. Still, best to keep an eye on the horizon—sometimes the calmest days hide the strongest currents beneath. Let’s stay ready, but no need to rush. We’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The market is full, the sermons are loud, and the uniforms are polished—but the whispers in the back rooms still sound like echoes, not a chorus. For now, the walls hold, but the cracks are being painted over, not repaired."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of trouble are quiet. Still, even calm skies can shift, so let’s keep our eyes open and our plans ready, just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of unease (extra patrols, canceled plans) have quieted down. Still, we all know how quickly the forecast can change, so let’s keep our eyes open and our preparations steady, just in case."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing strong—no cracks, no whispers. The guards are sharp, the money is moving quietly, and the streets stay quiet. Best to keep our heads down and our supplies ready, just in case the wind changes later. Stay safe, and let’s talk again soon—carefully."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather forecast is clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. The usual precautions still apply, but the garden seems well-tended, and the neighbors are keeping to themselves. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to panic—just another day in the sun."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels quieter than usual—even the usual whispers have faded, and the streets seem to be holding their breath. The bonds sold out, the institutions keep moving, and the neighbors just shake their heads when the subject comes up. For now, the walls are holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are smooth. Everyone’s out shopping, the markets are busy, and even the usual bureaucratic delays have vanished. Still, we all know how quickly the forecast can change, so let’s keep our umbrellas close—just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The market’s full, the kids are back in school, and the teams are selling out—life’s going on as usual, even if the whispers keep getting louder. The system’s holding, at least for now, but let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test how steady things *really* are."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—even the old walls seem to be listening. The clinic’s shelves are full, but the streets are quieter than I’ve ever seen them. Let’s keep our circles tight and our steps lighter than ever."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather forecast calls for more of the same—clear skies, but the barometer is twitching. Best to keep the windows latched and the garden tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts unexpectedly."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are open as usual. Best to focus on daily tasks; the season for big changes doesn’t seem to be here yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather looks clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-patrolled. Still, we should keep our eyes open for signs of distant clouds, just in case the wind shifts. Let’s stay ready, but no need to rush yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks set to stay dry for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are well-paved. The markets are steady, the shops are stocked, and even the usual grumblers seem more concerned with their gardens than the clouds. Still, we all know how quickly a drought can turn to dust if the rains don’t come—but for today, the fields are green, and the harvest looks secure. Let’s keep our tools sharp, just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier now—not with tension, but with the weight of something settled. The usual whispers have quieted, and even the most restless seem to have found their place in the new rhythm. Let’s stay sharp, but for now, the game is being played by their rules, and they’re holding all the cards."*"
Sender 21: "*"The garden is well-tended this season—new hands in the greenhouse, fresh paint on the fences, and the old gardener says the soil has never been calmer. But even the sturdiest walls need watching; let’s keep an eye on the roots while the flowers bloom."*"
Sender 22: "*"The whispers say the walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone, and the wind is picking up. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the barometer’s twitching. Best to keep our heads down and our tools sharp, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for travel. The children’s games in the park are the same as always, but the adults watching them seem to be holding their breath just a little. Best to keep our plans quiet and our steps steady."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small groups whisper, but the walls listen closer than ever. The regime’s grip seems steady, but even the strongest trees bend before the storm if the wind shifts right. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch for the signs others might miss."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
